Title: Knicks' Tyler Kolek: 'There's definitely a lot left for me to show'
People: Andrew Wiggins,3268;Joel Embiid,2611;Tyler Kolek,11;Tyler Kolek,1154;Tyler Kolek,1195;Tyler Kolek,2911;Tyler Kolek,3024;Tyler Kolek,4957;Tyler Kolek,4990;Klay Thompson,3231;Dillon Jones,3939;Giannis Antetokounmpo,3215;Scott Taetsch Getty,1174;Scott Taetsch Getty,1319;Mitchell Robinson,3812;Jeff Chiu,4976;Jeff Chiu,5057;Sarah Stier Getty,3003;Sarah Stier Getty,3125;Mike Brown,900;Bam Adeabayo,3251;Jalen Brunson,339;Tyrese Maxey,2626;Jose Alvarado,567;Tom Thibodeau,846;Ariel Hukporti,3924;Lebron James,2251;Kawhi Leonard,3349;Jaylen Brown,2266
Article_Text:
Tyler Kolek is in quite the situation.
On one hand, the third-year guard out of Marquette is an NBA champion, part of the stacked Knicks roster responsible for ending New York City’s 53-year championship drought in a 4-1 gentleman’s sweep of the San Antonio Spurs in June.
On the other hand? The Knicks are loaded at Kolek’s position.
Jalen Brunson is the reigning Finals MVP — the newfound King of New York City. Miles McBride is a flamethrower and defensive stopper at the guard spot, though McBride is up for a contract extension. And the Knicks traded for Jose Alvarado at last season’s deadline then re-signed him to a three-year deal this summer.
That’s three proven guards ahead of Kolek in the depth chart, meaning for a third straight season, minutes project as scarce at the pro level. Kolek averaged 7.2 minutes in 41 games as a rookie under Tom Thibodeau and 11.7 minutes in 62 games in Year 2 under Mike Brown. He averaged 4.4 points and 2.7 assists on 38.6% shooting from 3-point range as a sophomore but knows on a veteran Knicks roster looking to become the first team to repeat as champs since the 2018 Golden State Warriors, his role is to stay ready.
“I just gotta play my game everyday,” Kolek said to a small group of reporters while hosting a youth basketball clinic with FlexWork Sports at The House of Sports in Ardsley on Saturday. “Be consistent, whatever the coaches need just follow their direction and let it be what it is.”
Kolek isn’t in control of his minutes.
He is, however, in control of what he does with the opportunities he gets, however limited, for an NBA champion looking to protect its throne. Kolek knows there’s much more to his game than he’s been able to display in short stints over his first two NBA seasons.
“There’s definitely a lot left [for me to show],” he said. “Every year I try and get better. That’s how it’s been since college, year over year from my first year in the NBA and last year, the improvement. Now I’m just looking forward to improving on that.”
FAVORITES NO MORE
The ticker tape that once fell from the Champions Way skies is now sewage waste. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown went to Philadelphia, and so did the Eastern Conference championship projections.
Kolek helped the Knicks win it all last season. He then watched firsthand as the balance of power in the East shifted around them: The Sixers are now considered among many as favorites to win the conference with James and Brown joining Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and V.J. Edgecombe.
“I think you can take anything and use that to light a fire under you, anything you can use to be motivated, but at this stage, we shouldn’t have to be motivated. We’re champions,” Kolek said. “We know what it looks like, and we’re not just satisfied with one.”
The Sixers weren’t the only Eastern team to make big moves. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson joined Bam Adeabayo and Andrew Wiggins in Miami, and the Toronto Raptors traded for Kawhi Leonard, backed out of the trade in the wake of his salary-cap circumvention scandal, yet are still in play to trade for him again.
“It happens every year in the NBA. The [Oklahoma City] Thunder won the year before, and everybody loaded up to try to beat the Thunder,” said Kolek. “We win, it happens every single year. It’s a copycat league. Teams are trying to beat the best and compete with the best, so they do what they can.”
And then there’s the elephant in the room: Mitchell Robinson and the Knicks couldn’t agree to a deal, so he left New York and went to Boston. Plus Ariel Hukporti and Dillon Jones left the Knicks for the Sixers. Kolek is excited for a front-row seat to see Knicks All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns go to work against his former teammate.
“The longest tenured Knick, [Mitch] was great for us. His impact on the floor was tremendous, but that’s how this business works,” said Kolek. “Him going to Boston definitely hurts, big rivalry team, but we’re looking forward to catching him — I’m looking forward to seeing what KAT does when we play against him.”
STEALING FROM JALEN
While Alvarado frequently steals from the opponent, Kolek is looking to take from the captain.
The third-year guard said he got off to a strong start to his second NBA season before he became too passive on the offensive end. His offseason efforts on the court have revolved around improving his ability to make plays in the paint.
“Just looking for my shot, being aggressive in the paint, and then that opens everything else up,” he said, “having the defense collapse and then finding sprays for our guys.”
Kolek invoked Brunson’s name when discussing the improvements he hoped to make entering Year 3.
“Mostly in the paint, playing off two, obviously Jalen’s amazing in the mid-range, the floaters, finishing at the rim,” he said. “So I feel like just taking that aspect of the game as a smaller guard, being efficient in the paint and around the rim.”
Kolek may have already stolen another page out of the captain’s book: composure following an emotional championship run in the Mecca of Basketball. The Knicks will receive their rings on Oct. 20, ahead of tipoff against the very 76ers team aiming to take their throne.
“I think the first game will feel like a great celebration, but internally, you’ve gotta block out all the things the fans are saying, and the things the media is gonna say,” Kolek said. “Even though we’re not picked to be the favorites, New York fans are still gonna say we’re the champs. But we gotta stay locked in on our habits and focus on what we’ve gotta do every day.”

Title: Penn State notes: Rocco Becht entertains about 500 relatives, friends in win
People: Tony Roja,2674;Rocco Becht,70;Carson Hansen,2780;Finn Furmanek,3486;Nittany Lions,883;Quinton Martin Jr,2928;Yvan Kemajou,2315;Gabe Burkle,3447;Ben Brahmer,1046;Matt Campbell,1702;Kolin Dinkins,1194;Max Granville,1466
Article_Text:
PHILADELPHIA — Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht smiled when he was asked Saturday how much support he had in the crowd of 61,714 at Lincoln Financial Field.
Saturday was a “home” game for Becht, whose father, Anthony, grew up in Delaware County and starred at Monsignor Bonner High School. He estimated that he had hundreds of relatives and friends in attendance.
“I apparently had a lot (of support),” Becht said. “I was told there were about 500 people here from my dad’s side. There are probably people I haven’t met yet. It was great to have all those people here and to have them come out and support me. I appreciate all of them.
“I’ll probably see a lot of them when I walk out to the bus.”
Becht entertained them, completing 21-of-27 passes for 268 yards and three touchdowns and leading No. 16 Penn State to a 27-9 victory over Temple.
In his brief Nittany Lions career, he has completed 75.6% of his passes for 539 yards and seven touchdowns.
Two of his touchdown passes against the Owls (1-1) were 23-yarders to tight end Ben Brahmer, one late in the second quarter that gave Penn State a 10-3 lead and the second in the fourth quarter two plays after former Lions defensive back Kolin Dinkins hit him out of bounds after a 12-yard run.
“I’ve been playing with Rocco for three or four years,” Brahmer said. “I just know what he’s thinking and what his reads are on every play. I usually know when the ball’s coming to me.”
Granville out for year: Penn State defensive end Max Granville, who missed last season with a knee injury, suffered another serious injury during practice several days ago and will be out for the rest of the year.
“Obviously it’s a really tough blow for our football team,” Lions coach Matt Campbell said, “and most importantly a really tough blow for Max. He’s been a pillar of glue for the unity of our football team over the last nine months.
“That’s why we’re all really convinced that he’ll come back better than ever. It’s a tough loss for us. It was a tough day for us.”
Granville had a pass breakup and a quarterback hurry last week against Marshall. He played in seven games as a true freshman in 2024 after committing to Penn State as a four-star prospect from Sugar Land, Texas.
He was at Saturday’s game in street clothes.
“Max is a great teammate, a great player and a great friend,” said defensive end Yvan Kemajou, his roommate. “His injury affected us a lot. Seeing him go through that again, it stinks. We’re all here to support him.”
Running game: Penn State gained less than 5.0 yards per rush for the second time in as many games, finishing with 148 yards on 34 carries (4.4 average).
The Lions had a first down at the Temple 5 in the first quarter after Tony Rojas’ interception. They netted 3 yards on 3 attempts before Becht threw a fourth-down incompletion.
Carson Hansen ran 19 times for 84 yards for Penn State, James Peoples had seven carries for 42 yards and Cam Wallace gained 2 yards on his only run. Quinton Martin Jr. did not carry the ball after gaining 38 yards on 10 attempts last week.
“I feel like I probably felt last week,” Campbell said. “We’re like a hair off on some things. I thought there was good growth. I thought we were really physical at the point of attack.
“The team that we want to be and the team that we were today are still not equal. We have to be better. We have to demand it. We have to coach it better.”
Jumbo packages: Penn State often used four tight ends with the first appearance of the season by Gabe Burkle.
Brahmer, Rappleyea and Finn Furmanek also were part of those packages. Brahmer, who had five receptions for 79 yards, and Rappleyea, who had one for 5 yards, were the only tight ends with a catch.
“Gabe is such a great blocker,” Campbell said. “He’s a real challenge in the passing game, as well. Rap was awesome again. He sprung the huge play (Hansen’s 13-yard run in the third quarter).
“Those guys can do a lot of things. It allows you to get into formations and personnel stuff that gives you an advantage.”

Title: Knicks seem ready to take fans' worst Mitchell Robinson fear head-on
People: Mike Brown,1482;Mitchell Robinson,521;Ian Begley,883;James Dolan,241;Andre Drummond,953;Ariel Hukporti,620
Article_Text:
The New York Knicks won the NBA Championship for the first time in 53 years, setting their fans worldwide up for an entire summer of elation. That party lost some of its luster after just four days, though. That's how long it took team governor James Dolan after Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals to declare on WFAN's The Carton Show that it would be "basketball suicide" to enter the 2026-27 regular season over the salary cap's second apron.
The organizational refusal to pass that budgetary limit led directly to the loss of center Mitchell Robinson, previously the team's longest-tenured player, to the Boston Celtics. Ariel Hukporti leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers left the Knicks with just Karl-Anthony Towns at center. While the big man emerged as a superstar-level player throughout New York's championship run, everyone needs some sort of backup.
According to SNY's Ian Begley, the Knicks are reportedly high on the duo of Towns and Andre Drummond to get the job done at center. The "strong degree of confidence internally" in the pairing signals that, even if the front office adds another center ahead of the regular season, they don't plan on Brown having to depend on them very much. Especially as the rest of the league deals with second apron-induced losses of their own, the Knicks seem comfortable betting on their talent to be enough to survive the loss of Robinson.
Knicks have the personnel to live without a third big. Will they use it?
Last season, Mike Brown worked schematically to get Towns away from having to protect the rim as often. The reduction in reliance on traditional center play helped the All-NBA big man impact winning, on both ends of the court, more than ever before.
Drummond could benefit from a similar formula, with Brown counting on the big man's physicality to dissuade drivers and letting wing defenders like Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby, and even Miles McBride do the rest. Even if the X's and O's work out, though, the 33-year-old big man has missed 61 games over the past two regular seasons. Towns, who tends to get himself in foul trouble, will need more support.
One potential option would be to deploy Anunoby in spurts at the center position, an adjustment both of the team's recent head coaches have made in times of need. Exposing the wing to enough bumping and bruising down low, though, could come with other consequences with regard to his own availability.
The Knicks will have some tough choices to make next season. They know which five players to start and which players coming off of the bench will likely be most important to a win. But as of now, Anunoby is effectively their only answer to a scenario that involves Towns and Drummond dealing with injuries, foul trouble, or both.
How much faith in that duo does Rose really have?

Title: Knicks still have another drought to end next season even after winning a title
People: Carmelo Anthony,348;Neemias Queta,2311;Joel Embiid,1652;Nick Nurse,1809;Anfernee Simons,1787;Julius Randle,2356;Mitchell Robinson,2209;Mike Woodson,374;Jayson Tatum,2140;Lebron James,1600;Kawhi Leonard,1908;Jaylen Brown,1585;Jaylen Brown,2108
Organizations: New York Knicks,19;Minnesota Timberwolves,1056;Atlantic Division,297;Atlantic Division,638;Atlantic Division,778;Atlantic Division,826;Atlantic Division,1310;Atlantic Division,2436;Cleveland Cavaliers,1947;Oklahoma City Thunder,997
Article_Text:
The New York Knicks finally ended a 53-year championship drought this past season, after raising the Larry O'Brien Trophy for the first time since 1973. Now, they'll look to end another drought—albeit one of slightly less significance.
It has been 13 years since the Knicks last won the Atlantic Division. It happened in the 2012-13 season, Carmelo Anthony and head coach Mike Woodson led their group to a 54-28 record and the second seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs.
As the reigning champions, many might expect the Knicks to be the clear favorites to win their division in 2026-27. It certainly won’t be easy, though, as the Atlantic Division—at least on paper—looks to be the clear best of the six in the NBA.
Reigning NBA champions but not reigning Atlantic Division champions
Last season, the Atlantic Division went a cumulative 220-190. That was the best in the Eastern Conference and second-best in the NBA, only behind the Northwest Division, which features the Oklahoma City Thunder, Denver Nuggets, and Minnesota Timberwolves. Four of the top seven teams in the East came from the Atlantic.
Although they went on to win the NBA Finals, the Knicks finished second in the divisional race in 2025-26, three games behind the Boston Celtics. New York has won five Atlantic Division titles in franchise history (1970-71, 1988-89, 1992-93, 1993-94, and 2012-13).
As good as the Atlantic was last season (aside from the Brooklyn Nets), the division looks to be even better in 2026-27.
The Philadelphia 76ers have added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. While health—particularly with Joel Embiid—is a concern, their healthy starting five is arguably the best in the league. Adding players such as Dean Wade and Anfernee Simons also gives Nick Nurse more options off the bench.
The Toronto Raptors are (eventually) reacquiring Kawhi Leonard. The team took the Cleveland Cavaliers to seven games in the opening round of the playoffs last season and has a higher ceiling with Leonard.
The Boston Celtics no longer have Jaylen Brown, but they will have Jayson Tatum all season long. Boston also signed Mitchell Robinson away from the Knicks, who will give them a solid center combo for 48 minutes alongside Neemias Queta.
The Nets? Well, they added Julius Randle, but it would be shocking if they were near any of the other four Atlantic Division teams in the standings.
So, it will be tough sledding for the Knicks to end their division title drought. One major sportsbook lists New York as the favorite to win the Atlantic at +160. Both Philadelphia and Boston are close behind at +225. The Raptors are +800, with the Nets an absolute long shot at +50,000.
As the Knicks proved last season, though, they can reach another level once the playoffs arrive. It wouldn't be surprising if New York once again doesn't win the Atlantic—but they would still be quite the postseason threat.

Title: Astros announce latest update on Yordan Alvarez's injury ahead of Rays game
Article_Text:
Yordan Alvarez will not be in the Houston Astros’ lineup Friday night as the team opens a big series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Alvarez is getting a day off, but there is more to the decision than rest. The Astros slugger tweaked his ankle during Thursday’s game against the Philadelphia Phillies, according to Chandler Rome.
MORE: Bo Bichette’s future with Mets gets an update ahead of Yankees series
That makes the injury worth watching as Houston begins its series against the Rays. The Astros have not indicated that Alvarez is dealing with a serious injury, but his ankle could be the reason he is being kept out of the lineup.
Alvarez played Thursday in Philadelphia before sitting out Friday’s game. The timing gives him a chance to recover before the Astros decide how he will be used next.
The 29-year-old has been one of Houston’s most important hitters this season. He entered Friday hitting .310 with 38 home runs and 96 RBIs.
He is also chasing a possible Triple Crown. Alvarez entered the day near the top of the American League in batting average, home runs and RBIs.
His recent power has dipped, though. Alvarez has hit only three home runs since the beginning of August. That makes his health another concern for an Astros team trying to secure the AL West.
Houston entered Friday at 75-72 and is holding at least a three-game lead in the division. The Rays, meanwhile, own an 87-59 record and are leading the AL East.
The Astros will need to be careful with Alvarez during the final weeks of the season. His bat is too important to risk making a minor ankle issue worse.
For now, the team appears to be taking the cautious route. Alvarez is out Friday, and his ankle will be something to watch as Houston’s playoff push continues.

Title: Another View: Don't let Washington confuse you about vaccines. Talk with your pediatrician – Marin Independent Journal
Organizations: Department Of Health,817;American Academy Of Pediatrics,3844;Tribune Content Agency,3876;American Academy Of Pediatric,2853;United States,66;United States,1501;United States,2053;Human Services,834
Article_Text:
In August, we reached another grim milestone in the United States: Two deaths from measles were confirmed in Pennsylvania.
These losses are a painful reminder that measles is still deadly and that the consequences of falling vaccination rates are measured in people’s lives. For pediatricians, the lives of our patients — children and babies — are our immediate concern.
It is heartbreaking to witness deaths from a disease that is preventable with a vaccine that has been widely used since the 1970s, helping to have eliminated domestic cases of measles by 2000. What families need today is strong, steady leadership from the U.S. government, in partnership with the medical community, to urge MMR vaccination for all who are eligible. Instead, the president and the secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services are spreading falsehoods about vaccines, delivering chaos and confusion to families rather than clarity and reassurance.
In fact, earlier in August, President Donald Trump signed an executive order calling for fewer routine childhood vaccines but more doctor’s visits to space out shots. As a pediatrician for more than 30 years, I can tell you plainly: This makes no sense.
Particularly troubling against the backdrop of the recent measles deaths in Pennsylvania, the order also suggests that parents should receive separate vaccines for measles, mumps and rubella instead of the combined MMR vaccine. These separate vaccines are not even currently available in the United States, and even if they were, substituting them for the combined vaccine would lead to more appointments for parents, more individual shots for young children, greater costs to families and more unnecessary expense to the healthcare system.
There is no medical reason to split up or space out these shots – none. At a time when measles is spreading across the country and many children remain too young to be vaccinated, we should be making it easier for children to get immunized, not harder.
All of the noise coming from Washington is part of a political agenda that has nothing to do with how doctors evaluate research and offer advice to their patients. When politicians give credence to false messages about vaccines, children and their families pay the price.
Right now, U.S. children are going back to school with kindergarten vaccine rates continuing to decline nationally, an indicator that many communities do not have enough people vaccinated to stifle outbreaks. The consequences are real: Measles cases have reached a 35-year high in the U.S.
I want to reassure parents that as of today, nothing has changed for your family. The vaccines pediatricians recommend for children today are the same ones they needed a few weeks ago, and they are still available and still covered by insurance.
The American Academy of Pediatrics’ 2026 immunization schedule — the one backed by over a dozen major medical organizations — still recommends routine childhood vaccination against about 18 diseases, including measles, influenza, RSV, hepatitis A and B, rotavirus and meningococcal disease. Children in the U.S. who are up to date on their vaccines, are better protected today than any time in history.
The advice I’ll share here is the same advice pediatricians are giving parents across the country: Be sure your back-to-school checklist includes a conversation with your pediatrician. Ask whether your child is up to date on recommended immunizations. Ask why certain vaccines are given at specific ages. No question is too small.
As pediatricians, we are here to listen to your concerns and support you as you make decisions about your child’s health. Our advice, as always, is based on what’s best for children’s health and well-being, not politics.
Dr. Andrew D. Racine is president of the American Academy of Pediatrics. ©2026 Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

Title: Bill Maher Destroys the Left Over 9/11, and It's Brilliant
Article_Text:
After 9/11, everyone promised to “Never Forget.” The surge of patriotism that rose from the wreckage in New York, Pennsylvania, and the Pentagon was remarkable, albeit short-lived. Somewhere along the line, a large swath of Americans did, in fact, forget. And you know what side of the aisle did the forgetting.
Of course, we’ve been saying as much on the right for years. But this week there was criticism from the left, when Bill Maher marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11 on his show. He spent it calling out everyone who has spent the last quarter-century pretending not to remember who did the killing: the left. His own side.
Maher opened by thanking the Americans who kept the country safe for 25 years after the attacks, then pointed out how much has changed since. "Back then we were against the terrorists," he said.
Maher walked through exactly how the country got there. He noted how four journalism associations issued guidance telling reporters that "terrorism should only be used in quotes because it's emotionally and politically loaded. He also cited Canada's state media CBC, which instructs reporters, "Do not refer to the September 11th attacks as terrorist attacks," and the BBC, which told its own staff the word "terrorist" can be "a barrier rather than an aid to understanding."
It would be funny if it weren’t true.
ICYMI: Greg Gutfeld Reflects on 9/11, and You Really Need to Watch This
That refusal to name the enemy, Maher argued, is a symptom of something much bigger: the American left quietly switching sides in a fight it once understood perfectly well. He framed the post-9/11 world as a genuine clash of civilizations between radical Islamism and Western liberalism, and pointed out how many people who call themselves liberal have ended up rooting for a side that hates freedom of religion, hates gay people and treats women as property.
"How did liberals wind up on their side?" he asked.
Is it a fair question? You bet it is.
And there’s no use in pretending that this isn’t exactly what’s happening. In fact, as Maher pointed out, 20% of young Americans now hold a positive view of Osama bin Laden, whom he dubbed “Luigi Mangione in a turban."
Maher tied that moral confusion directly to Gaza and to the leftists who have made it their current cause. He tore into the casual use of the word "genocide," calling it "an easily provable lie.” And yet he backed it up with facts that leftist activists conveniently ignore: Israel moved 94,000 truckloads carrying more than 1.8 million tons of aid into Gaza, and let more than 36,000 patients leave for treatment abroad.
Let’s be honest, what Maher was really describing was a party that has decided a terrorist regime deserves the benefit of the doubt America itself never gets.
Gaza was just the pretext.
Maher's deeper point is that toppling the systems that built the West is the actual leftist project, and Gaza happens to be this new fashionable excuse for it. He called it the Democrat Party's worst moment since it abandoned Reconstruction.
It’s sad that this is what has become of the left. The 9/11 attacks were awful, but what the left is doing to this country is worse, because it’s coming from within.
The prevailing view of so much of the young left in America is that we’re the worst country ever, so if someone attacks us, they can’t be all bad. pic.twitter.com/u01HsCRnv3
— Bill Maher (@billmaher) September 12, 2026
Twenty-five years ago, honesty about who attacked this country wasn’t controversial. Maher's monologue was a rare reminder from inside liberal media that a terrorist is a terrorist, no matter how uncomfortable the label makes the snowflakes in the media or the Democrat Party.

Title: Penn State overcomes slow start to beat Temple behind Becht, Brahmer
People: Tony Rojas,1424;Carson Hansen,968;Andrew Rappleyea,1650;Ryan Barker,1766;Ben Brahmer,338;Rocco Becht,276;Jeremiah Cooper,2390;Nittany Lions,161;Matt Campbell,136;Jaxon Smolik,1493
Article_Text:
PHILADELPHIA — Penn State looked sluggish Saturday in the first quarter of its first road game in the Matt Campbell era.
The Nittany Lions found themselves in a tie late in the second quarter against three-touchdown underdog Temple. That’s when Rocco Becht delivered a 23-yard touchdown strike to tight end Ben Brahmer, which propelled No. 16 Penn State past the Owls 27-9 before an announced crowd of 61,714 at Lincoln Financial Field.
The Lions scored on five consecutive possessions to erase any thought of history repeating itself. On their last visit to Philadelphia in 2015, they lost to the Owls for the first time since 1941.
“Who responded? The guys you’d expect,” Campbell said. “Our A players made big plays in A moments and made A plays, which is what you hoped would happen in adverse situations.”
Becht completed 21 of 27 passes for 268 yards and three touchdowns. The 6-7 Brahmer caught five throws for 79 yards and two TDs. Carson Hansen carried 19 times for 84 yards.
Becht and Brahmer have played together since 2023, the first three seasons at Iowa State and now at Penn State. They have a special connection.
“We’re always on the same page,” Becht said. “Knowing he was going to break in, that’s just repetition from the reps we’ve gotten the past three years. He’s a really great player to have and to throw to. It’s great to have him on our side.”
Penn State defenders made big plays, too.
Linebacker Tony Rojas intercepted a pass thrown by former Penn State teammate Jaxon Smolik in the first quarter. Rojas returned it to the Temple 5, but the Lions didn’t score. Three runs netted 3 yards, and Becht’s fourth-down pass to tight end Andrew Rappleyea was incomplete.
Penn State ran 12 plays inside the Temple 20 in the first 22 minutes without scoring. Ryan Barker, who led the nation in accuracy last season, missed a 33-yard field goal try before making two kicks later.
“We didn’t play very well offensively in the first quarter,” Campbell said. “If you go back and look at those three runs in the red zone, they’re all there. The first one is a bad run. The second one we get beat on the inside and the third one we get beat at right guard (Cooper Cousins).
“When you play on the road, you have to have great execution,” Campbell said. “Then defensively, we gave up two 40-yard plays because of a lack of detail.”
The first one was a 47-yard run by Smolik, who broke a tackle by safety Jeremiah Cooper. Temple (1-1) had a first down at the Penn State 5 and had to settle for a field goal and a 3-0 lead.
“That was big,” Campbell said of keeping the Owls out of the end zone. “It was huge. I thought our response when our backs were against the wall was awesome.”
Penn State took command, starting with Barker’s first field goal. Becht found wide receiver Chase Sowell on a screen for a 16-yard touchdown and hit Brahmer for another 23-yard score in the fourth quarter.
“I thought it was a good game for us to have,” Becht said, “to be humbled after a good win. Playing against a good team like Temple, we just started off a little slow. We made the adjustments after the first quarter and at halftime.
“We were a lot better in the second half. We needed this before we begin conference play.”

“Obviously it’s a really tough blow for our football team,” Lions coach Matt Campbell said, “and most importantly a really tough blow for Max. He’s been a pillar of glue for the unity of our football team over the last nine months.
“That’s why we’re all really convinced that he’ll come back better than ever. It’s a tough loss for us. It was a tough day for us.”
Granville had a pass breakup and a quarterback hurry last week against Marshall. He played in seven games as a true freshman in 2024 after committing to Penn State as a four-star prospect from Sugar Land, Texas.
He was at Saturday’s game in street clothes.
“Max is a great teammate, a great player and a great friend,” said defensive end Yvan Kemajou, his roommate. “His injury affected us a lot. Seeing him go through that again, it stinks. We’re all here to support him.”
Running game: Penn State gained less than 5.0 yards per rush for the second time in as many games, finishing with 148 yards on 34 carries (4.4 average).
The Lions had a first down at the Temple 5 in the first quarter after Tony Rojas’ interception. They netted 3 yards on 3 attempts before Becht threw a fourth-down incompletion.
Carson Hansen ran 19 times for 84 yards for Penn State, James Peoples had seven carries for 42 yards and Cam Wallace gained 2 yards on his only run. Quinton Martin Jr. did not carry the ball after gaining 38 yards on 10 attempts last week.
“I feel like I probably felt last week,” Campbell said. “We’re like a hair off on some things. I thought there was good growth. I thought we were really physical at the point of attack.
“The team that we want to be and the team that we were today are still not equal. We have to be better. We have to demand it. We have to coach it better.”
Jumbo packages: Penn State often used four tight ends with the first appearance of the season by Gabe Burkle.
Brahmer, Rappleyea and Finn Furmanek also were part of those packages. Brahmer, who had five receptions for 79 yards, and Rappleyea, who had one for 5 yards, were the only tight ends with a catch.
“Gabe is such a great blocker,” Campbell said. “He’s a real challenge in the passing game, as well. Rap was awesome again. He sprung the huge play (Hansen’s 13-yard run in the third quarter).
“Those guys can do a lot of things. It allows you to get into formations and personnel stuff that gives you an advantage.”

Title: Courteney Cox thriller tells 'dysfunctional love story' behind pizza bomber case at TIFF | 100.7 MIX-FM | Today's Hit Music

Article_Text:
By Ryan Patrick Jones
TORONTO, Sept 12 (Reuters) – Courteney Cox’s true crime thriller “Evil Genius” recounting the infamous U.S. pizza bomber case premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on Saturday.
The film, starring Academy Award winner Patricia Arquette and “Stranger Things” actor David Harbour, is the “Friends” star’s first feature film as a director in 12 years, following the 2014 black comedy “Just Before I Go.” It is based on the 2018 Netflix documentary series “Evil Genius: The True Story of America’s Most Diabolical Bank Heist.”
The movie centers on the convoluted plot in which pizza delivery man Brian Wells robbed a PNC Bank near Erie, Pennsylvania, in 2003 with a homemade bomb locked around his neck. The device detonated after his arrest, killing him.
Arquette plays Marjorie Diehl-Armstrong, a woman with bipolar disorder who was later convicted of the robbery. Prosecutors said she masterminded it to raise money to hire a hit man to kill her estranged father over an inheritance dispute.
Harbour co-stars as Bill Rothstein, her former fiancé and accomplice. His call to police – reporting the body of Diehl-Armstrong’s boyfriend James Roden in his freezer and implicating her in the killing – broke the case open.
Cox said on the red carpet she was drawn to the story by the unusual relationship between Diehl-Armstrong and Rothstein.
“There’s a dysfunctional love story that’s really the catalyst for this heist,” Cox said at the premiere. “There were some really humorous moments and also tragic, but I just thought ‘I’m going to walk the line, tell the story with a tone that’s … not identifiable with any specific genre.'”
Arquette said she strove to capture what motivated Diehl-Armstrong, who died in prison in 2017.
“Oftentimes, people who are bad guys, they don’t really see themselves as that. They have their reasons why that person’s their enemy, or that person let them down, or they should have that thing, or how the world screwed them over,” she said. “Understanding those underpinnings, I think, was the most important to me.”
(Reporting by Ryan Patrick Jones in Toronto; Editing by Alistair Bell)

Title: Los mapas muestran predicciones del follaje de otoño de 2026. ¿Cuándo alcanzarán su punto mayor los colores?
Article_Text:
A medida que se acerca el primer día del otoño, el 22 de septiembre, la atención se centra en los colores vibrantes y hermosos que pronto lucirán las hojas.
De hecho, la temporada de observación de las hojas ya casi está aquí, ya que el calor abrasador del verano llega a su misericordioso final.
La mayoría de las áreas de EE. UU. tendrán colores máximos entre finales de septiembre y mediados de octubre, aunque el momento exacto depende de la ubicación y varía de un año a otro según las condiciones climáticas previas al otoño, según AccuWeather.
¿Dónde estará el mejor vistazo a las hojas?
“Seguimos pensando que la mejor observación del otoño se realizará en partes de la región de los Grandes Lagos y la parte superior del Medio Oeste unido con el septentrión de Pensilvania, el septentrión de Nueva York y el septentrión de Nueva Inglaterra”, dijo el meteorólogo de AccuWeather Alex DaSilva a USA TODAY.
Anuncio
Anuncio
Dijo que estas áreas, especialmente en las partes interiores del noreste, pudieron escapar de las peores condiciones de sequía de este verano.
El plano muestra el pronóstico de cuándo alcanzarán su punto mayor los colores del follaje de otoño en EE. UU.
Un plano de AccuWeather muestra cómo los colores del otoño alcanzarán su punto mayor en septiembre en el septentrión y se desplazarán cerca de el sur a medida que continúe el otoño:
Razones para el optimismo en Nueva Inglaterra
Para Nueva Inglaterra en particular, hay muchas razones para ser optimistas, según la revista Yankee. Los bosques afectados por la sequía del año pasado produjeron una temporada de follaje breve y acabado. Pero un invierno frío y nevado, una rico humedad primaveral y lluvias oportunas en verano han reabastecido los suelos y ayudado a que los bosques se recuperen, afirmó la revista.
Los árboles en gran parte de la región están entrando a finales del verano con copas exuberantes y saludables y relativamente poco daño generalizado por insectos u hongos, según el corrido diestro en follaje Jim Salge de la revista Yankee.
Anuncio
Anuncio
El resultado, dice Salge, podría ser una temporada muy diferente a la de 2025, con el color llegando más gradualmente y permaneciendo más tiempo a medida que avanza desde las montañas del septentrión hasta la costa sur de Nueva Inglaterra.
“Nuestro llamado anticipado para 2026: un aparición sosegado podría preparar el proscenio para una temporada de follaje larga y espectacular”, dijo Salge en un correo electrónico a USA TODAY.
La sequía “perjudica los colores vibrantes”
Según DaSilva, la sequía puede practicar una presión significativa sobre los árboles, y las sequías prolongadas pueden ser perjudiciales para los colores vibrantes. “Es por eso que esperamos que partes del sureste estén aburridas este año. Las sequías más prolongadas, especialmente en las Carolinas y Georgia, han provocado que los árboles se estresen”, dijo a USA TODAY.
Otra ámbito donde la sequía probablemente causará condiciones más aburridas será en partes de las Montañas Rocosas, dijo DaSilva. La sequía es de severa a extrema en esta ámbito y eso puede provocar más estrés en los árboles.
Anuncio
Anuncio
“Otra cosa a la que tendremos que prestar atención es cualquier tormenta de derrota en otoño”, dijo. “Los fuertes vendavales pueden derribar las hojas antaño de tiempo y arruinar las condiciones de visualización vibrantes”.
Dónde el follaje de otoño podría conmover temprano o tarde
El momento del follaje de otoño podría variar tanto como la calidad de los colores, según el meteorólogo de AccuWeather Brian Lada, en un documentación en linde.
Lada dijo que donde los árboles ya están estresados, pueden perder sus hojas antaño de lo habitual, incluidas áreas desde Georgia hasta Nueva Pullover y en gran parte de las Montañas Rocosas. Las tormentas tropicales o los sistemas con ráfagas de derrota a finales del verano y principios del otoño todavía podrían originarse las hojas de los árboles antaño de que la temporada luces su pico característico.
“Mientras tanto, las condiciones más cálidas podrían retrasar el cambio estacional en otras regiones. Los días cálidos en todo el valle de Ohio y partes del valle de Mississippi pueden retrasar la caída de las hojas un par de semanas, mientras que los días y noches cálidos en el noroeste podrían retrasar el cambio aproximadamente una semana”, dijo Lada.
Anuncio
Anuncio
El follaje de otoño pico debería conmover según lo previsto en otras partes del país, incluido el noreste, los Grandes Lagos y las Llanuras del Boreal.
Más: ¿Inteligente para percatar que es otoño? Aggiornamento del pronóstico a medida que los días se acortan
¿El cambio climático está afectando el follaje de otoño?
¿Qué papel tiene el cambio climático en el momento del follaje de otoño? Un diestro tiene una respuesta:
“Los registros históricos, las observaciones satelitales y los experimentos nos dicen que el momento del follaje de otoño generalmente se retrasa en respuesta al aumento de las temperaturas asociadas con el cambio climático”, dijo Amanda Gallinat, profesora asistente de estudios ambientales en Colby College, en un correo electrónico de 2024 a USA TODAY.
Anuncio
Anuncio
“Aquí en Nueva Inglaterra, el pico de follaje ocurre hasta una semana más tarde, en promedio, que en la lapso de 1950”, dijo.
Doyle Rice es corresponsal franquista de USA TODAY, especializado en tiempo y clima.
Este artículo apareció originalmente en USA TODAY: Los mapas muestran predicciones del follaje de otoño de 2026. ¿Cuándo alcanzarán su punto mayor los colores?

Article_Text:
People fleeing Iran-backed rebels' advance in Yemen describe a 'hysterical panic'
Houthi rebels backed by Iran have made a swift advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast, causing thousands to flee. The Associated Press on Saturday spoke with some of those on the run. Some residents of Aden, under Yemen's internationally recognized government, are opening their homes to the displaced. The United Nations warns the escalating fighting could lead to a humanitarian catastrophe and return to civil war. The rebels' advance also threatens a key global shipping route as they now perch at the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Meanwhile, Iraq says the attack that closed a Saudi oil pipeline originated from its territory.
Saudi Arabia has few options as it faces mounting threats from Iran and its allies
Houthi rebels in Yemen are advancing toward a crucial trade chokepoint. Attacks blamed on Iraqi militias forced the closure of a major pipeline. Iran and its allies are unleashing a nightmare scenario for Saudi Arabia and unsettling global markets. Control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could allow the Iran-backed rebels to cut off another major export route for Saudi oil as Iran disrupts the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudis could use U.S. support to fight back. But President Donald Trump seems reluctant to widen an already unpopular and stalemated war in the Middle East.
US diesel prices soar past $6 a gallon, deepening strain for hauling everyday goods
CHICAGO (AP) — Diesel prices in the U.S. has hit yet another record, soaring past $6 a gallon on average as Washington’s war with Iran disrupts the world’s flow of fuel. The national average of nearly $6.06 is up from $5.85 last week and almost $3.71 from this time last year, according to motor club AAA. Higher diesel prices mean more expensive transportation for a long list of everyday goods. That’s because diesel is used for many freight and delivery networks. And some businesses have already passed along steeper costs to consumers in the form of added fees.
Mississippi police arrest a man in the death of Tasia Fortune
Mississippi police have arrested a man in the death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman found hanging from a tree last month. Police in Jackson told reporters Friday that the man was arrested after the state medical examiner’s office determined Thursday evening that the death was a homicide. Police discovered Fortune’s body hanging in the backyard of an abandoned home on Aug. 3. The police say the case is active and more warrants will be pending. Fortune’s mother says the family is in shock and still doesn't have a lot of answers. She says police did not share a motive or whether DNA led them to the arrest.
Trump touches a nerve while in Ireland by saying reunification would be 'fantastic'
DUBLIN (AP) — President Donald Trump has touched a political nerve by saying a unified Ireland would be “fantastic.” The American leader is on a weekend trip for a golf tournament at the Doonbeg course he owns in Ireland. In Dublin, thousands of people turned out in protest. Trump met with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Dublin. He expressed support for unifying the Republic of Ireland with Northern Ireland. It's a sensitive topic due to historical tensions and violence. Previous U.S. presidents have avoided direct comments on the issue. Trump also met Irish President Catherine Connolly. Trump’s son Eric says the Trump family is loved in Ireland.
BRICS leaders voice concern over Middle East, condemn unilateral sanctions at India summit
NEW DELHI (AP) — Leaders of the BRICS nations have expressed concern over rising tensions in the Middle East and condemned sanctions not authorized by the U.N. The leaders met in New Delhi on Saturday to strengthen their global position. In a statement indirectly criticizing U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, they have voiced concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities. The leaders have also opposed unilateral sanctions, with Russia facing Western sanctions after its invasion of Ukraine. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasized that BRICS is not against the West but seeks a greater voice for developing economies.
8 killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine as Putin warns Europe against sending troops
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russian strikes have killed eight civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, according to local officials. President Vladimir Putin has warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would mean direct conflict with Russia. Ukraine faces mounting pressure from Russia's intensified air campaign. Moscow's attacks target Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter, aiming to demoralize civilians. Putin, speaking at the BRICS summit in India, denied that Russia poses any threat to Europe. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that he would meet Putin if both leaders were invited to the Group of 20 summit in December in Miami.
US marks 25 years since the Sept. 11 attacks
NEW YORK (AP) — The U.S. is commemorating the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks that left nearly 3,000 people dead and the nation shaken. On Friday, people laid wreaths, flew flags, read victims' names and held moments of silence and vigils. In 2001, attackers took command of four commercial jets and rammed them into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. On Friday, President Donald Trump attended a ceremony at the Pentagon. Former Presidents George W. Bush, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama and Joe Biden and current Vice President JD Vance went to ground zero in New York, where victims’ relatives read aloud the long list of names. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum laid a wreath at the Flight 93 National Memorial in Pennsylvania.
FACT FOCUS: A look at false and misleading claims during the Republican midterm convention
President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other Republican officials came together for a two-day convention this week to rally voters in advance of midterm elections in November. But in celebrating their accomplishments, they made several false and misleading claims, many of which have been stated repeatedly during Trump’s second term. They covered topics including the economy, healthcare and the 2020 election.
No relief from inflation as Middle East clashes lifts fuel prices to painful levels
WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas prices spiked in the wake of renewed fighting in the Middle East, underscoring the affordability challenges that are top of mind for many voters as midterm elections near. The Labor Department said Friday that the consumer price index rose 3.4% last month compared with a year ago, the same as in July. But on a monthly basis, inflation accelerated, as costs jumped 0.4% from July to August, up from an increase of just 0.1% the previous month. The figures show that inflation remains stubbornly elevated, more than five years after prices first soared as the economy emerged from the COVID pandemic.

Title: Aztecs lose backup quarterback to broken collarbone
People: Bert Emanuel Jr,417;Jayden Denegal,322;Charlton Luniewski,719;Draiden Trudeau,273
Article_Text:
PASADENA — San Diego State backup quarterback Stone Saunders is expected to miss the next six to eight weeks following surgery this week for a broken collarbone suffered in last week’s victory over Portland State, sources told the Union-Tribune.
SDSU redshirt freshman Draiden Trudeau replaced starting quarterback Jayden Denegal in the final two minutes of Saturday’s 28-10 loss to UCLA at the Rose Bowl, throwing an incomplete pass on his only attempt. Quarterback-turned-wide receiver Bert Emanuel Jr. was the Aztecs’ emergency quarterback.
Saunders was injured on a sack in the final minute of SDSU’s 53-20 victory over Portland State. The play, a fourth-and-1 attempt on PSU’s 1-yard line, was SDSU’s final offensive play of the game.
Saunders reached for a high snap from backup center Charlton Luniewski and had the ball bounce off his hands and above his head.
As Saunders waited for the ball to come down, Portland State safety Lono Solomon rushed in untouched from the edge. Solomon wrapped his arms around Saunders and landed on top of the Kentucky transfer as he hit the turf on his right shoulder.
Saunders did not appear pained when he got up, although his right arm hung to his side as he walked off the field. He had surgery on Wednesday, according to sources, and did not accompany the team on Saturday’s road trip.
Saunders is a former four-star high school quarterback from Pennsylvania who set state passing records during his prep career. He was among SDSU’s most coveted transfers from the January portal period after redshirting at Kentucky.
Saunders took over for Denegal in the fourth quarter against Portland State. He completed 2 of 4 passes for 20 yards.
Trudeau is a redshirt freshman walk-on from Mission Viejo whose primary role has been quarterbacking the scout team in practice. Trudeau had not appeared in a game for the Aztecs.
Dorje booms ball
SDSU punter Tashi Dorje picked the right moment for his career-long punt. Standing at the back of his own end zone with nine minutes remaining in the first half, Dorje boomed the ball 77 yards to the UCLA 19-yard line.
The punt was aided by a fortunate bounce past UCLA returner Mikey Matthews. Dorje actually outkicked his coverage, as they say. Matthews ran down the ball and returned it 22 yards before he was tackled.
Dorje also had 55-, 43- and 50-yard punts in the first half, giving him a 56.3-yard average. He finished the game with seven punts and a 50.0 average.
The 77-yard punt was the ninth-longest in SDSU history. The Aztecs now have six punts of at least 77 yards since 2021 (Matt Araiza, 4; Tyler Pastula, 1; Tashi Dorje, 1).
Select company
The 0-0 first half between SDSU and UCLA was a rare event.
There were 941 FBS games last season between the regular season (887) and postseason (54).
Only two of those games were 0-0 at halftime: Jacksonville State-UCF in Week 0 and Miami-Texas A&M in the College Football Playoff.
Sutton on all-time rush list
SDSU running back Lucky Sutton is on the verge of moving into the Aztecs’ all-time top 20 rushing list. Sutton had 19 carries for 81 yards in the first half, giving him 1,636 for his career. That put him within 28 yards of Art Preston (1,664 from 1949-51), who currently ranks 20th all-time for the Aztecs.
Coming up
SDSU plays James Madison on Saturday at 7 p.m. at Snapdragon Stadium.
James Madison set a school record for points Saturday in an 87-3 home victory over Wagner, going 21-21-24-21 across four quarters.
The Dukes rushed for 290 yards and six touchdowns and returned two punts for TDs.
Quick hits
• While SDSU’s 45 passing yards against UCLA were low, the Aztecs threw for only 14 yards in a 40-13 win over Utah State in 2016.
• The Aztecs had 14 first downs in the game, nine rushing, one passing and four on penalties. The one passing first down came on Denegal’s 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jackson Ford. It was SDSU’s longest offensive play of the day.
• Linebackers Sione Hala and Tano Letuli each had eight tackles, sharing team-high honors in the category with safeties Jelani McLaughlin and Josh Hunter.
• SDSU’s Nathan Acevedo muffed the first punt of the game, but Hunter covered the ball to prevent the Bruins from getting it at the SDSU 10-yard line.
• The Aztecs’ longest possession was a nine-play, 30-yard drive that consumed 4:37 in the first quarter. They had four three-and-outs among 11 possessions and had an average time of possession of 2:16.
